why-ninja: Every preset here uses Ninja, including on Windows, and that is a considered choice rather than a taste.
The Visual Studio generator drives MSBuild, and MSBuild loads whatever is integrated user-wide on the machine.
On the Windows box this port was done on, vcpkg is integrated that way and is broken: a probe build failed with
'pwsh.exe' is not recognized, from a vcpkg MSBuild target, in a project that does not use vcpkg at all.
Ninja never loads that machinery, so the build depends on the compiler and on nothing else.
Ninja is also single-config, which is what makes the RelWithDebInfo default in CMakeLists.txt meaningful.
windows-prerequisites: Configure from a 'x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2022' (or run VsDevCmd.bat first).
That is what puts cl.exe, the Windows SDK and the right LIB/INCLUDE on the environment.
Visual Studio ships a Ninja next to its CMake, at
and the developer prompt puts it on PATH. That path is deliberately NOT hardcoded here: it names one edition
(Community) and one install location, and a preset that only works on one machine is not a preset.
If 'cmake --preset windows-msvc-debug' cannot find ninja, you are not in a developer prompt.
toolchain-floor: MSVC must be 19.35 or newer (Visual Studio 2022 17.5) for /experimental:c11atomics.
CMakeLists.txt checks this and fails with that message rather than letting it become a C1189 deep in a header.
engine-only-builds: bbengine and morgue-tests do not need JUCE. With third_party/JUCE empty, configure still succeeds,
prints a warning, and gives you a buildable engine and a runnable test suite.

That is the fast loop: cmake --build --preset

--target morgue-tests && ctest --preset
